content_html:
Since 2010, I've written an annual "year-in-review" blog post0. It has been nearly two years since I quit my job and went into the FIRE, so what has life been like and have I achieved everything I dreamt of?

Life has been pretty chill! I've been reasonably relaxed, seen loads of shows and gigs, travelled around the world a bit, hung out with cool people, and had no major issues with… well, anything. I've got back into using FourSquare / Swarm to track the places I've been to - that's rather fun.

I've ticked off a lot of things I wanted to do - including some interesting new dining experiences.

I haven't done everything I wanted though. My good friend Jessica introduced me to the concept of New Year's Bingo Boards. Twenty-five things that you want to accomplish over the year. I made it 12 completed and two half-completed. That's not bad - but I must do better.

OKR, KPI, O4Q

How did I do against last year's goals? I'm not so into the "quantified self" - all I really record is the beers I drink and the number of steps I take. But let's look a bit more high-level.

  • Bits and pieces of work.
    • Yup! A handful of clients, and I landed a grant. I'm not doing brilliantly at being retired 🤣 but it keeps me out of mischief.
  • Attend - but don't speak - at conferences.
    • Yup! Went to a whole bunch of conferences and just enjoyed myself. They're a lot more fun when you're not panicking about a talk!
  • More health - more exercise.
    • Keeping to a respectable weight. Taking care of some health issues - oh the joys of getting old(er)! - and trying to prevent more.
  • Travelling.
    • An epic two-month Interrail trip, plus a week at the Edinburgh Fringe, plus a few other trips. Exhausting but fun!
  • Shows and Gigs
    • A dozen plays, half a dozen gigs, then all the shows at Edinburgh. Oh, and I've started reviewing shows for a new website. Culture is pretty great, innit?
  • Keep blogging.
    • Hey, you're reading this, aren't you? I now tend to blog every other day unless there's a burning issue I can't wait to write about.
  • See more friends in person.
    • Smashed it out of the park, mate! Saw loads of people. 100% recommend chatting shit with your buddies.

On To The Next Year

Do I need to set goals for myself? Without any external motivation, I find it a bit too easy to drift. I should track what I'm doing, but probably don't need to be all quantified-self about it.

So, here's an attempt at a list. Tune in next year to see how it went!

  • Finish what I start.
    • I have a lot of projects on the go. Time to make sure they're done and put away.
  • Learn to solder.
    • I went to a terrible soldering class a while ago and it right put me off. I've bought a bunch of stuff, now working up the gumption to learn what I'm doing without burning down the house.
  • Spend more time with friends.
    • I hate making plans. It takes effort and it's often very easy to sit on the settee eating crisps. Perhaps I should invite people over to eat crisps?
  • Document more.
    • I realise that lots of the smarthome & tech stuff we have only exists in my head. I probably ought to write it all down.
  • Try some new stuff.
    • That's a bit vague, innit? What else is out there for me to experiment with?

The 2025-2026 series has gone smoothly, no major plot twists and no-one has been re-cast. What will next year be like? Set a reminder to be back here same blog-time, same blog-channel.

All just a little bit of history repeating

Previously on the Terence Eden adventures…

2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018, 2017, 2016, 2015, 20141 2013, 2012, 2011, and 2010.

  1. Today is my birthday - so this is when the new year starts for me. ↩︎

  2. The year 2014 is relegated to a pocket universe and can only be accessed in case of emergency. ↩︎
